source_note: Highest anneal temperature in the compiled SiC rows (Nipoti et al., microwave anneal). Set from the dataset itself; SiC sublimation and decomposition onset lies well above typical anneal temperatures.
Approximate temperature below which activation is generally reported to be poor; no single primary source.

Regime change in GaN decomposition: Rebey et al., J. Cryst. Growth 1999 (10.1016/s0022-0248(99)00081-0) report activation energies of 1.87 eV below and 0.38 eV above 830 C. Rana et al., MRS Proc. 743, 2002 (10.1557/proc-743-l11.28) find no decomposition up to 800 C and a near-amorphous surface by 1100 C. Both are near-ambient-pressure studies, not the 1 GPa UHPA conditions used for Mg activation.
Highest anneal temperature in the compiled GaN rows (Hirukawa et al. isochronal series under UHPA). UHPA raises the ceiling by suppressing N loss.
Commonly cited low-doping Al acceptor level in 4H-SiC; no primary source attached.
Commonly cited approximate Mg acceptor level in GaN; no primary source attached.

Sakurai et al. 2019 APL (10.1063/1.5116866) and Sakurai et al. 2020 ISPSD (10.1109/ispsd46842.2020.9170174) both state that conventional RTA causes serious GaN decomposition even with an AlN cap, and that 1 GPa N2 UHPA suppresses it.

All SiC anneals in the dataset (furnace, microwave, Si overpressure) are at or near atmospheric pressure, up to 2100 C. This difference in process regime from GaN is why anneal temperatures are normalized per system.

Anchors: Fontaine et al. 1996 APL (10.1063/1.115879) anneal at 1450 C (10 min) after cold implantation and in-situ heating at 1050 C; Vogel et al. 2004 (10.1016/j.diamond.2004.04.005) anneal up to 1650 C. Graphitization risk depends on dose, fluence and depth rather than on a single ceiling temperature, so the value is an illustrative central estimate.
Seki et al. 2023 pss(a) (10.1002/pssa.202300522) give 0.3 eV as the expected ionization energy of substitutional B in diamond; Seki et al. 2025 JAP report 0.38 eV in the light-doping regime.
Diamond B-implant anneals in the dataset are furnace or in-situ heating at ambient pressure; the accessible range (up to ~1450-1650 C) lies between GaN's atmospheric limit and SiC's.
